captions.threads:
1/4 you're laughing at something funny and suddenly you're watching yourself laugh from three feet away. like you're observing your own life instead of living it. this is supposed to feel like you. why doesn't it?

2/4 the disconnection isn't a bug in your system. it's actually a really smart protection mechanism your nervous system installed when things got too loud or too much or too chaotic. dissociation is your brain saying "i'm going to step back here for a second." which is reasonable. which also sucks.

3/4 so you're stuck in this weird space where the protection saved you but now you're running your whole existence from behind glass. you can see everything happening. you just can't feel like you're in it. the frustration makes total sense because you're grieving access to yourself while also kind of needing that distance to survive.

4/4 the reframe isn't "get rid of it." it's recognizing that reconnection starts with curiosity about why you left in the first place. what made stepping back feel necessary? that's not a flaw to fix instantly. that's information. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/i-feel-disconnected-from-myself

entries.postTitle: I Keep Choosing Comfort and Regret It Later

captions.threads:
1/4 comfort is a liar that tells the truth. it feels so good in the moment that you actually believe the relief is real. you skip the hard thing at 2pm. you feel fine at 2:15pm. this is the trap. the regret doesn't show up until 11pm when you're alone with what you didn't do.

2/4 comfort doesn't feel bad. that's the whole architecture of the trap. if avoiding the thing made you feel terrible immediately, you'd stop doing it. but it doesn't. it gives you 20 minutes of genuine ease and then vanishes. by then the choice is already locked in.

3/4 i used to think i was weak. turns out i was just really skilled at negotiating with myself. "i'll do it tomorrow" isn't laziness, it's a deal your nervous system cut without asking permission. the real problem isn't comfort. it's the quiet, repeated betrayal that follows.

4/4 the actual reframe: comfort and regret are the same transaction. you're not choosing between them. you're just choosing which one hits first and which one you're willing to carry. the discomfort now, or the hollow feeling at midnight. the choice was always about timing, not avoidance.

Sit with this one.

Your AI tools can optimize a caption down to the last emoji, but they can't tell you whether you're actually saying anything true. We're building increasingly sophisticated systems to chase engagement metrics, but the automation layer is making it easier than ever to delete the weird line, the opinion, the real thing. What if the next frontier isn't smarter tools but the courage to stay human when the algorithm rewards polish over realness?

INSTAGRAM:
your thumb hovers. you cut the weird line. the engagement gods smile.

You know the moment. Right before you post something you actually made, something that matters. You reread the caption. Then you edit out the real part because it feels too raw, too weird, too much like actually you.

#authenticity #creators #creatorlife #neurodivergent #artistlife #keepitreal #yourselfmatters

THREADS:
1/4 Approval and authenticity are not the same thing, and we've stopped treating them like opposites when we should be treating them like enemies. Every day I watch creators, musicians, and neurodivergent entrepreneurs choose the safer version of themselves online. The algorithm rewards it. Our followers expect it. So we deliver it. And we die a little smaller each time.

2/4 That moment before you post, your thumb hovers over the weird line. The one that actually says something. The one that feels too strange, too personal, too much like revealing who you actually are. So you cut it. You soften the opinion. You reshape your voice into something acceptable. And you tell yourself it doesn't matter because you got the post out anyway.

3/4 But there's a tax on this trade-off that nobody talks about. The more you choose approval, the harder it becomes to hear your own voice. You start forgetting what you actually think beneath the layers of what you think people want from you. Your creative work becomes documentation of a persona instead of expression of a person.

4/4 The weird line isn't a liability. It's the only thing that makes your work yours. When you cut it, you're not editing for clarity. You're editing for invisibility. captions.threads:
1/4 The piece that absolutely demolishes you at 11pm while scrolling is not always the piece you'll still love in daylight. I learned this the hard way. That urgent "I NEED this now" feeling is real, but it's not always truth. Sometimes it's just the algorithm's timing meeting your nervous system at exactly the right (or wrong) moment.

2/4 So I started doing this thing: screenshot it. Let it sit. Come back three days later and see if the resonance is still there or if it evaporated like a dream you can't quite remember. The pieces that survive this waiting period? Those are the ones actually speaking to something in me, not just my dopamine.

3/4 Your gut knows things your scrolling brain doesn't. But your gut also gets confused by novelty and stimulation and the feeling of scarcity. The waiting period isn't about killing the spark. It's about letting the real connection separate from the urgency, so you can actually trust what you're choosing.

4/4 This applies to way more than art, by the way. Anything you're buying into, committing to, believing in. Give it the three-day test. See which resonances stay loud when the scroll spiral settles.
